name: Fishing
intro: Where the bite forecast matches the water and the map works offline, and where an update hides the core feature behind a subscription.

apps.title: FishWeather: Marine Forecasts
apps.verdict: It's a go-to app for wind and marine conditions before heading out, with a reputation for accuracy that whole angling communities like Maine lobstermen rely on. It's weaker on wave height, which people call inaccurate, and water temperature is basically missing. The sore spot is that once-free things like the offshore report and the waves tab got moved behind a subscription or removed entirely, and against intrusive ads that angers even paying users.
apps.loved: Accurate wind forecasts, being ready for sea conditions before a trip, trust from entire coastal communities, monthly pricing
apps.weak: Inaccurate wave height, no water temperature, features moved behind a subscription or removed, intrusive ads, crashes
apps.whoFor: Offshore and coastal anglers who care most about wind and safe conditions to go out

apps.title: Fishdope Fishing App
apps.verdict: This is a narrowly specialized service for saltwater fishing in Southern California, and dedicated boaters love it: fresh bite reports, water temperature and chlorophyll charts, spotter-plane fish scouting, all of which saves them hours and hundreds of dollars in fuel. The weak spot is the barrier to entry: the app is nearly useless without a paid subscription and without internet, and some content (zone reports, certain species) is trimmed in the app versus the website. Beginners and anyone outside SoCal will get little from it.
apps.loved: Fresh bite reports from top captains, water temperature and chlorophyll charts, spotter-plane fish scouting, fuel and time savings, showing your position relative to temperature breaks
apps.weak: Nearly useless without a paid subscription, requires login and internet, zone reports and some species trimmed in the app versus the website, useful only for Southern California
apps.whoFor: Serious saltwater anglers and private boaters in Southern California willing to pay for fresh fish scouting

quotes.text: It has put us on the fish or in the general vicinity trip after trip. If you live in Southern California and have a boat, it is an absolute no-brainer.
reports on species such as island based white sea bass, barracuda, or even island based yellows is very limited and sporadic.

apps.title: Fishing & Hunting Solunar Time
apps.verdict: Long-time users trust the solunar forecast and find it accurate for bass, reds and trout. The weak spots are specific: a lifetime purchase is lost when you switch from Android to iPhone, the calendar sometimes will not let you pick a date, and the default location resets to Lebanon, KS. The activity percentage also sometimes disagrees with what you see on the water.
apps.loved: Accurate solunar forecast proven over years, helps pick your time on the water, kids like the graphs, responsive support
apps.weak: Lifetime purchase lost when switching from Android to iPhone, the calendar sometimes will not let you pick a date, default location resets to the wrong city, the activity percentage sometimes disagrees with reality
apps.whoFor: Experienced anglers and hunters who trust a solunar calendar and want to pick the best time to head out

quotes.text: There’s some days I go hunting and it 90% and I don’t see a deer and then there’s days when it’s 18% and I see deer. I understand that the app uses moon’s phases but try to be better.

apps.title: Omnia Fishing: Spots & Maps
apps.verdict: Its strength is accurate lake maps with depth contours that genuinely help find deep holes and spots without wasting time, and support is responsive. The lack of offline hurts badly: many lakes have no signal and the app is useless there. A separate headache is the store side, items are perpetually out of stock, plus billing surprises after a supposedly free trial and intrusive AI all over the interface.
apps.loved: Accurate lake maps with depth contours, finding deep holes and spots without wasting time, responsive support, tackle inventory feature
apps.weak: No offline where there's no signal, store constantly out of stock, unexpected charges after the trial, AI all over the interface
apps.whoFor: Freshwater bass anglers and kayakers who read depth maps and also buy tackle

quotes.text: Really like all the features on the app. But it did not cover many of the in Iowa so it was not very beneficial to me. If it covered all the lakes I fish I would have kept it, without a doubt.
Most lakes I go to there is no internet. I can’t use this app while I’m there! Kind of useless

apps.title: Fishing Forecast - TipTop App
apps.verdict: For those it suits, people like the bite forecast by time and species and being able to save favorite spots, handy for a beginner deciding when to go. It breaks down on coverage: for some, after subscribing there is no data at all in their area, and the navigator is kilometers only. Note that many five-star notes are generic and some reviews look planted.
apps.loved: Forecast of the best bite time by species, saving favorite spots, helping a beginner decide when to go, a lot without a subscription
apps.weak: No data in some users' area even after subscribing, glitchy screens, navigator in kilometers only, at times confusing interface, inaccurate rain forecast
apps.whoFor: A beginner angler who just wants to know the best time to head out, if their area has data.

apps.title: Salt Strong: Fishing Spots App
apps.verdict: People praise it as an all-in-one for saltwater: tides, wind, bite score, ready-made spots and a log that auto-fills tide and moon, and people genuinely started catching more. It breaks down on performance: it lags badly, overheats the phone and drains battery a percent a minute, and some get stuck at sign-in entirely. Plus smart spots are generic and incomplete in some states.
apps.loved: All-in-one for saltwater, log auto-filling tide and moon, ready-made spots and route planning, genuinely catching more fish
apps.weak: Lags badly and overheats the phone, drains battery a percent a minute, gets stuck at sign-in, daily updates, smart spots generic and incomplete outside Florida, expensive
apps.whoFor: An inshore saltwater angler, especially in Florida, who wants an all-in-one and can tolerate the lag.

quotes.text: Finding spots, marking spots, private catch log with all details automatically filled in (tide, moon, spot, etc), tracker, route planning - it’s the only tool that gives you 100 percent of what you need.

apps.title: Fishing Knots FishPlanet
apps.verdict: People really do learn new knots from the pictures and value the selection. But the teaching is weak, too few steps for a beginner, and some diagrams are simply wrong, for example the uni knot and perfection loop breakdowns. The lack of search and ads that stay even after a paid yearly subscription make it worse.
apps.loved: Teaches new knots, good knot selection, simple clear pictures, handy to keep on the water
apps.weak: Too few steps for beginners, some knot diagrams are wrong, no search or sorting, ads remain even after paying
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want to quickly look up or learn a knot and can tolerate ads and basic teaching

apps.title: Deep Dive - Bass Fishing App
apps.verdict: People genuinely plan their trip around this app: it pulls wind, waves, water clarity and dam release schedules into one place, which rivals don't do. It breaks on coverage: a couple of popular lakes like Guntersville are packed with detail while your home water shows nothing, and water clarity often goes stale for days. Almost everything useful sits behind a subscription that people struggle to cancel.
apps.loved: Breaking down a lake before a trip, wind and wave forecasts, dam release schedules, environmental data rivals lack
apps.weak: Blurry satellite imagery, water clarity rarely updates, patchy regional coverage, useful data locked behind subscription, hard to cancel billing
apps.whoFor: Tournament bass anglers on popular reservoirs who prep the night before and don't mind paying for a subscription

quotes.text: Love this app! I can break down my lake faster (there’s water clarity, wind/wave forecasts, dam schedules, etc.) Helps me make a solid game plan the night before. Advanced environmental data that no other app has - best on the market.
You must membership to use. The one free bait they show is always a top water for every condition.

apps.title: Fishing Deluxe - Best Fishing Times Calendar
apps.verdict: A years-long favorite calendar of best fishing times: people praise the accuracy of bite peaks, the simplicity, and no endless add-on purchases unlike competitors. There's exactly one problem, but a serious one: the current version crashes every time you open the map or change location, and the weather block stopped loading. On iPad the app crashes immediately. The developer is silent, so an otherwise excellent app has become nearly useless.
apps.loved: Accurate bite peaks, accuracy proven over years across states, simplicity, no pushy add-on purchases, handy for planning short trips around the bite
apps.weak: Crashes when opening the map or changing location, weather block won't load, crashes immediately on iPad, no longer works with Apple Watch after updates, developer silent
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want a simple accurate calendar of best bite times without extra purchases, if they can survive the map bug

quotes.text: Very accurate and useful I fish about 100 days a year and peak fishing times are truly helpful

apps.title: FishAngler: Fishing Guide App
apps.verdict: People kept a log, chatted and praised the accurate forecast and peak bite times for years. But the March 2026 update locked other people's catches and peak times behind payment, and that used to be the main free value. Add sign-in failures, a stuck login and stale catch reports up to five years old, and many left.
apps.loved: Accurate forecast and peak bite times, catch log, chatting with anglers, some features stayed free
apps.weak: The March 2026 update locked other people's catches and peak times behind payment, sign-in failures and endless loading, stale catch reports up to five years old
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want a forecast and a log and will now pay for what used to be free

quotes.text:
I was very disappointed in the catch reports on the lakes and rivers. Most of the reports were five years or older.
Seems there are not many people repo
After years of contributing and using FishAngler as a community tool for anglers all over the world, the March 2026 update that paywalls seeing other peoples catches has killed the app for me.

apps.title: iSolunar™ Hunt & Fish Times
apps.verdict: People value it for solunar hunt and fish times and for being a one-time purchase with no subscription, and matching the classic Alden Knight paper tables wins over the old guard. The weak spot is the add-on weather module: people pay for it separately, yet wind, direction and temperature don't work after purchase. A separate pain is that the app forgets the purchase and restoring access just spins and never completes, plus updates lose trophy photos and there's no pinch-to-zoom.
apps.loved: Solunar hunt and fish times, one-time purchase with no subscription, matching classic Alden Knight tables, simplicity
apps.weak: Broken add-on weather module, app forgets the purchase and won't restore access, lost photos after updates, no pinch-to-zoom
apps.whoFor: Old-school hunters and anglers who trust solunar tables and don't want subscriptions

apps.title: Fish Deeper - Fishing App
apps.verdict: This is the app for the Deeper castable sonar ball, and people love it for being compact: handy from a kayak instead of a full-size fish finder, helps target spots where fish actually are rather than empty water. But the phone connection drops, especially below 50% battery or more than a couple of feet away, the signal is delayed and jumpy, and you can't open the bathymetric map until you've mapped 70% of the lake, which is impossible from a kayak. Many are also annoyed that after subscribing the app keeps pushing them back to the payment page.
apps.loved: Compact, handy from a kayak, accurate on the narrow beam for finesse fishing, helps find fish, saves time
apps.weak: Phone connection drops especially below 50% battery, delayed and jumpy signal, can't open depth map until 70% of lake is mapped, keeps asking for subscription after paying
apps.whoFor: Owners of a Deeper sonar on a kayak or boat who want portable fish-finding without a fixed fish finder

quotes.text: Super easy to use while on the kayak and a great alternative to having to mount a full-size finder
I have the PRO+ it’s loses connection when when the phone is 3 feet from the bobber. Also when it is connected the data is delayed and jumpy. The readings are not smooth.

apps.title: Fishing Points: Map & Forecast
apps.verdict: People praise the app for tides, saving spots and a catch log, and some think it is more accurate than rivals. But for inland lakes there is often no depth or chart data even though it is promised, and the activity forecast and wave heights disagree with reality. Plus unpleasant charges up to 49.99 dollars, sometimes even during the trial.
apps.loved: Tides, saving and organizing spots, catch log, fish species identification, accuracy above many rivals
apps.weak: No depth charts for inland lakes despite the promise, activity forecast and wave heights disagree with reality, lots of ads, blind charges up to 49.99 dollars
apps.whoFor: Coastal and offshore anglers who care about tides and organizing spots, less suited to inland lakes

apps.title: FishTrack - Charts & Forecasts
apps.verdict: The core value is finding warm water and temperature breaks before heading offshore, then punching the coordinates straight into a chart plotter. It stumbles on coverage: no Gulf of Mexico, bathymetry stops at southern New Jersey, images often fail to load. It's pricey at around 79 dollars a year, and one guide flatly says he gets the same data free from NASA Worldview.
apps.loved: Accurate sea surface temperatures, finding temperature breaks before a trip, coordinates straight into a chart plotter, monthly billing option
apps.weak: Poor bathymetry, narrow regional coverage, images often don't load, high price, trouble accessing paid features
apps.whoFor: Offshore anglers hunting temperature breaks who run a chart plotter

apps.title: onWater: Fishing Spots Map
apps.verdict: People praise that it feels built by anglers for anglers, handy for learning streams and rivers while traveling, with accurate flow-rate data. It breaks down on the free version where nearly every click asks for payment, and on the measurement tool that is buggy and rarely works. Plus map crashes and broken login for some.
apps.loved: Built by anglers for anglers, learning streams and rivers on trips, accurate flow-rate and weather data, finding nearby boat ramps
apps.weak: Nearly every click in the free version demands payment, buggy measurement tool, crashes viewing the map, inaccurate ramps and river miles, broken login for some
apps.whoFor: A stream-and-river angler who travels and scouts new waters and is willing to pay for a subscription.

apps.title: Hunt & Fish Times by iSolunar™
apps.verdict: The core, solunar tables and moon phases for predicting game and fish activity, works and lands with people: many say the data is close to the US Naval Observatory and actually matches animal behavior. What breaks is the extras: weather and wind direction are often wrong or won't load, the app crashes after updates, and support doesn't answer emails. A separate sore point is that it used to be a one-time purchase and is now a subscription.
apps.loved: Accurate solunar tables and moon phases, matches US Naval Observatory data, ease of use, helps predict deer and fish activity
apps.weak: Weather and wind often wrong or won't load, crashes after updates, support silent, moved from one-time purchase to subscription
apps.whoFor: Hunters and anglers who trust solunar tables and moon phases and want a simple bite forecast

apps.title: Fishbrain - Fishing App
apps.verdict: People really do find spots and log their catches, one user caught their first fish in El Paso thanks to Fishbrain. But what used to be free is now locked behind a roughly 155 dollar a year subscription: you cannot even see other anglers' catches and photos in the feed. That turned a useful tool into a wall of locks.
apps.loved: Finding fishing spots, catch logging, connecting with other anglers, planning trips to unfamiliar waters
apps.weak: Almost everything locked behind a pricey subscription, cannot view other people's catches and photos, the map confuses zoom with dropping a pin, laggy after updates
apps.whoFor: Beginners who need to find nearby spots and keep a catch log, and who will pay a subscription to see others' catches and lure tips

quotes.text: The app was originally amazing used to be able to see what catches other people caught at a spot. Now I have to pay the premium in order to see any catches that anyone is caught.

apps.title: Fishing Times Calendar
apps.verdict: It's a simple solunar bite calendar with an easy-to-read clock, which is what people love it for, some using it for years on Toledo Bend. The main trouble is in the core itself: the time display is broken, mixing 24-hour and AM/PM formats into things like '13:34 pm' that can't exist. On top of that many call the bite predictions inaccurate, one angler with 40-plus trips a year always gets a 'fair-to-poor day', and ads pop up right while you're planning.
apps.loved: Easy-to-read bite clock, simplicity, solunar times, 7-day outlook for free
apps.weak: Broken time display mixing formats, inaccurate bite predictions, ads while planning, confusion over free versus paid
apps.whoFor: Anglers wanting a simple solunar guide to bite times who tolerate rough predictions

apps.title: onX Fish: Midwest Fishing Maps
apps.verdict: People praise the fast way to find new lakes, access points and lakes with high populations of the fish they target, handy for a novice and for scouting. It breaks down on map detail: contours too coarse to pick out structure, many lakes simply missing, and depths wrong in places. Plus subscription pop-ups keep coming even after paying and state coverage is incomplete.
apps.loved: Fast finding of new lakes and access points, lakes with high populations of target fish, 3D maps and satellite, easy for a novice
apps.weak: Coarse contours with no structure detail, missing half the lakes Navionics has, depths wrong in places, subscription pop-ups even after paying, incomplete state coverage
apps.whoFor: A Midwest angler scouting new lakes who is fine with a general picture without detailed contours.

quotes.text: The lake depths is way off found a cove that was supposed to go from 4ft to 15 ft drop off the whole cove was 3 ft wasted time and gas uninstall

apps.title: Angler: The Fishing App
apps.verdict: The strength people stick with for years is the fishing journal: catch logs with photos, notes by fishing method, and a forecast of fish activity by time. Russian-speaking regulars praise exactly this. But the weather block simply doesn't work for many, showing a blank screen or a temperature off by 20-plus degrees, and tide times can be wrong. You also can't pick a specific spot on the water, and without paying you can't see tomorrow's forecast.
apps.loved: Fishing journal with catch log and photos, notes by fishing method, fish-activity forecast by time, simple clear layout
apps.weak: Weather broken or blank screen, temperature off by 20-plus degrees, tide times wrong, can't pick an exact spot on the water, tomorrow's forecast is paywalled
apps.whoFor: Anglers who value a detailed catch journal and a bite forecast by time and can live with broken weather

apps.title: Fishing Spots: Find & Fish App
apps.verdict: The app helps find new spots and share catches, and for some that is enough even without paying. But the peak bite times that were free for years were moved behind the subscription, and the forecast became hard to read. Sign-in failures, no live weather and plenty of fake catch coordinates that people post at random get in the way.
apps.loved: Finding new fishing spots, sharing photos and tips, some value stays free
apps.weak: Peak bite times moved behind the subscription, a forecast that is hard to read, sign-in failures, no live weather, fake coordinates on other people's catches
apps.whoFor: Anglers who mainly want to find new spots and share catches, if fake pins and paying for peak times do not bother them

quotes.text: I wish you could do something about people posting there pictures and then giving bogus locations of there catch! The app is called fishing spots but it’s obvious a lot of them are bogus!

apps.title: Fishbox - Smart Fishing App
apps.verdict: Where there is data, people praise the bite forecast for accuracy, and the free access to the AI stands out too. But for rivers and many lakes there is little or no data, and spot and bait tips that used to be free moved behind the subscription. A separate pain is charges during the trial and 27.99 dollars with no refund.
apps.loved: Accurate bite forecast where data exists, free access to the AI, help deciding where to go
apps.weak: Thin data for rivers and lakes in your area, inaccurate tide charts, charges during the trial with no refund, no way to judge the value before paying
apps.whoFor: People fishing popular areas with good data coverage who want a bite forecast, but are willing to risk paying blind

apps.title: Fishing App - Pro Angler
apps.verdict: People get it for the bite reports: what's biting, on what bait, with which techniques, and when reports are fresh they're valued. The catch is many have none: the last report dated June 20 when opened July 8, and without a subscription you get a generic description instead of a local report. Users also hit crashes when tapping the map, offer screens on launch, and instability searching for a new spot.
apps.loved: Specific bite reports by species and bait, social-style feed of catches, lots of data in one place
apps.weak: Reports often stale or missing, crashes when tapping the map, ads on launch, little works without a subscription, glitchy new-spot search
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want local bite reports and fish unfamiliar waters

quotes.text: With other apps, reports always felt vague or like ai, like they could apply anywhere. But Pro Angler gets specific. It tells you what species are biting, what bait is working, and even techniques that are worth trying.
No fishing reports on this app. When you try to pull up local fishing reports you only see a generic description of how the fish inshore and offshore.

apps.title: BUBBA Fishing
apps.verdict: People praise the scale itself, sturdy and handy for culling fish at a tournament. It is maddening that on top of a 60-99 dollar device they also charge 5 dollars a month for app features, and some of those do not work even after paying. Plus glitches: the screen freezes, auto-log fails to record a fish, the catch map gets the location wrong.
apps.loved: Quality and grip of the scale itself, easy fish culling at tournaments, storing trips and catches
apps.weak: Subscription on top of an already-bought scale, some features broken even after paying, the mid-tier model does not connect, screen freezes, auto-log fails, catch map mislocates catches
apps.whoFor: A tournament angler with a BUBBA scale who has accepted a monthly fee for catch tracking.

quotes.text: Trying to add a catch from two days ago, it lets me select the correct day and time but when it saves it, changes it to current date and time. Doesn’t save the location either.

apps.title: TroutRoutes: Fly Fishing App
apps.verdict: People value it for one thing: it opens up trout streams and access points you never knew existed, even near home. It breaks exactly where it matters most, on the water: the app hangs on a blue screen, demands a connection and won't open without cell data at the river, and offline is capped at 750 tiles. Coverage is very uneven nationwide, near-empty in Maine and Florida, all against complaints about price and post-update glitches.
apps.loved: Finding new trout streams and access points, spots near home, useful water-access data
apps.weak: Hangs on a blue screen, needs a connection at the river, 750 offline tile cap, uneven nationwide coverage, UI cut off at the edges
apps.whoFor: Fly anglers chasing trout who want new streams and water-access points in well-covered regions

quotes.text: I fish in Wisconsin’s driftless area where there’s limited cell service at times. That means no maps, etc to help orient to where you are. TroutRoutes must be satellite... No matter where I’m at, I can see in real time as I move upstream.
Offline maps are useless when you are limited to 750 tiles. Overall, you’re paying for the data.

apps.title: BassForce: Bass Fishing Guide
apps.verdict: People value the pro-level lure and condition tips, for a beginner it is a ready-made plan for the day. It breaks down on almost everything sitting behind a paid subscription, with the free version buried under payment pop-ups. Plus complaints about crashes when adding a location and wrong water temperature.
apps.loved: Pro-style lure advice, tips tied to water conditions, help for beginners choosing bait
apps.weak: Almost everything locked behind a paid subscription, pushy payment pop-ups, crashes when picking a location, inaccurate water temperature, no custom ponds or cross-device sync
apps.whoFor: A beginner bass angler willing to pay for lure guidance who does not want to work out conditions alone.

quotes.text: It tells you everything you need to know and the best part is ITS FOR FREE it tells you how pros would fish a certain type of structure what they would throw what the water conditions are the bait fish which bank the wind is blowing on
This app seems to give repeat lures, colors and size. It doesn't seem to matter the settings. I actually have never caught anything that this has suggested, but I do catch them every week.
It would be nice to see when a lure is selected how it is to be rigged or the preferred rigging technique. Would have 5 stars then.

apps.title: BassForecast: Bass Fishing App
apps.verdict: When it works, the lure tips genuinely help, people catch bass on the app's advice. But more and more often the app simply will not load, hanging on a grey screen, and ads are shown even to paying subscribers. Forecast accuracy is inconsistent, and the best baits of the day that used to be free were moved behind the subscription.
apps.loved: Lure tips that work, helps decide when and where to catch bass, a daily bite rating
apps.weak: Often fails to load and hangs on a grey screen, ads even for paying subscribers, inconsistent forecast accuracy, best baits of the day hidden behind the subscription
apps.whoFor: Bass anglers who want daily lure tips, if they can put up with loading failures and ads

quotes.text: I’m a little disappointed, there’s some good info and some good discounts and deals, but the peak times never seem to make sense for me. I don’t think I’ve even gotten a bite during these “peak times” which are almost always in the afternoon.

apps.title: Fishing Points - Lake Maps
apps.verdict: People value it as a cheap Navionics alternative after Garmin raised prices, it works for ice fishing and from a kayak and shows structure and currents. It breaks down on accuracy: depths off by several feet, GPS missing the mark, and some boats lose map detail after an update. Plus support does not reply and the one-time-versus-yearly purchases are murky.
apps.loved: Cheaper than Navionics, works for ice fishing and from a kayak, shows structure and drop-offs, tide and current data
apps.weak: Depths off by several feet, GPS off by dozens of yards, paid upgrade fails to deliver promised detail, support goes silent, confusing one-time and yearly map purchases, no legend
apps.whoFor: A budget angler on a kayak or ice who needs a structure map without Garmin's pricey subscription.

quotes.text: App doesn’t pinpoint my location accurately and the depths have been off by several feet which makes a big difference in smaller lakes.

apps.title: Fishing Calendar & Tide Times
apps.verdict: When it works, the best fishing times are accurate, and people spend years comparing them against the real bite. But the tides often do not work, there is no switch to a 12-hour time format, and the graph does not show all the hours of the day. Support stays silent, and some people did not renew.
apps.loved: Accurate best-fishing-time picks, a simple clear interface, helps you settle into a new region
apps.weak: Tides often do not work, no switch to a 12-hour time format, the graph does not show all hours of the day, support does not respond
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want a simple best-bite-time calendar and can tolerate broken tides

quotes.text: The times it tells you to go and the days are pretty accurate when I go to the lake and the bar is all the way up. I catch fish, but when it’s down, I usually don’t

apps.title: Lowrance: app for anglers
apps.verdict: People love the depth maps and being able to plan a trip at home, then push waypoints to the Lowrance sonar on the boat. Stability keeps breaking: crashes when opening the map, waypoints vanishing after a sync, freezes during basic navigation. They also removed the water-level adjustment that was the whole reason to pay.
apps.loved: Detailed depth maps, planning trips at home and pushing points to the on-boat unit, the shaded depth palette
apps.weak: Constant crashes and freezes, sync deletes waypoints, removed water-level adjustment, will not connect to Ghost and Live units, wrong weather, interface not made for boaters
apps.whoFor: An owner of Lowrance gear who plans trips ahead and transfers points to the sonar, if they can tolerate crashes.

quotes.text: When I go to the Lowrance app to add my ghost it just gets stuck on the loading screen. When I try to pair the trolling motor directly to my phone it doesn’t show up

apps.title: Fishing App: ANGLR Logbook
apps.verdict: The job people buy it for: keeping a fishing log, trip track and catch log tied to location, and the app even pulls photos from your camera roll and creates entries from them, which people love. But the latest update nearly killed it: starting a trip throws an error, logging a catch crashes the app roughly half the time, and this is even in the paid Pro version. Many write that development was abandoned for a couple of years while the subscription kept billing, and support is terrible.
apps.loved: Automatic catch log from camera-roll photos, trip track and mileage, marking spots along the bank, Apple Watch integration, ease of use
apps.weak: Frequent crashes after update even in Pro, starting a trip errors out, logging a catch crashes the app, development abandoned for years, terrible support
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want a detailed catch log with automatic photo parsing and trip tracking, if they can tolerate crashes

quotes.text:
Start a trip … error message though, it does start.

Log a catch … it crashes.

Restart app.

Log the catch a second time it will crash 50% of the time.

apps.title: Fish AI - AI Fishing App
apps.verdict: At its core the app helps a beginner find spots and figure out where to go for fish. But the path to any value is built like a trap, dozens of survey questions, then a promise of free access and a sudden charge of around 80 dollars a year with no monthly option. Many never saw the free access they were promised.
apps.loved: Finds fishing spots, suggests where to go and what fish to catch, handy for beginners, simple setup
apps.weak: A long survey leads straight to payment, promises free but charges around 80 dollars, no monthly option only yearly, almost everything locked until you pay
apps.whoFor: Beginners who want a simple spot finder, if they will pay a full year upfront without a trial

apps.title: FishVerify: ID & Regulations
apps.verdict: People like the idea, identify the species and get its regulations right away, and the fish info is good. It breaks down on the core job: identification often gets it wrong or does not see the fish in the photo at all, and for an offshore angler out of signal range it simply does not work. Plus everything hinges on a mandatory email login and identifications capped by credits.
apps.loved: Species identification with its regulations, good reference info on the identified fish, help in unfamiliar waters
apps.weak: Identification often wrong or fails to see the fish in the photo, does not work out of signal range, mandatory email login, identifications capped by credits, cannot add a fish to the log without a photo and an ID
apps.whoFor: An angler in unfamiliar waters with signal who needs regulations for the species they caught, if they can live with ID misses.

quotes.text: Gets the types of fish right, eventually. Even when you crop the photo super tight, it still takes a couple of tries to detect a fish.
The app sounds like a great idea, the problem for offshore fisherman out of cell range, when ID is needed for a fish the app cannot work. Wish it would!

apps.title: Fish | Hunt FL
apps.verdict: Florida's official wildlife app is valued for one thing: carrying your fishing license digitally on your phone instead of paper, plus rules, limits and a species identifier at hand. But people are furious that short 3 and 7-day licenses were removed, so out-of-state visitors now have to buy an annual one or stand in line for an hour at a tax office. On top of that the app crashes on launch and on iPad, the license often won't load, and tide and sunrise data are wrong versus NOAA.
apps.loved: Digital license on your phone, rules and limits at hand, species identifier, convenient for those always carrying a phone
apps.weak: Short 3 and 7-day licenses removed, crashes on launch and on iPad, license often won't load, tides and sunrise wrong versus NOAA, no way to add license to phone wallet
apps.whoFor: Florida anglers and hunters who need a digital license and state rules at hand

apps.title: Fishing Times Pro
apps.verdict: A simple solunar calendar of bite times: some rely on it for years, and wind readers like the handy wind forecast. But people are put off that the last major update stripped features and broke the interface, and many want the old version back. Plus data errors: tides in feet show as meters, the 24-hour format gets confused (12:16 becomes 24:16), and date scrolling stopped working.
apps.loved: Simple solunar bite calendar, handy wind forecast, easy location switching, years-long habit
apps.weak: Update stripped features and broke the interface, tides in feet show as meters, 24-hour time format confusion, date scrolling broken, paid version barely differs from free
apps.whoFor: Solunar-table believers who want a simple bite calendar and wind forecast and can tolerate data bugs

apps.title: LakeMonster: Fishing AI
apps.verdict: People genuinely value having the data in one place: water temperature, recent satellite imagery, live marina cameras and weather for planning a trip. But the headline feature, the AI fishing plan, is broken for days at a time, the app freezes to a white screen, and support answers neither emails nor the in-app form. Cancelling the subscription and getting a refund is also nearly impossible.
apps.loved: Accurate water temperature, recent satellite imagery, live marina cameras, all weather data in one place
apps.weak: AI plan broken for days, frequent crashes and white screen, support silent, can't cancel subscription or get a refund
apps.whoFor: Anglers who want water and weather data before hitting the lake and can tolerate a raw AI feature

apps.title: Fishidy: Fishing Maps App
apps.verdict: Valued for depth maps with contours and structure points, a social feed of other people's catches, and a long history (some since 2012). But many complain that after paying you hit a loop of problems: premium won't unlock, the map loads only vegetation or a white screen, and for the lake or river you actually need there's simply no data. Plus few active people in the feed, so fresh catch reports are almost nonexistent.
apps.loved: Contour depth maps and structure points, social catch feed, long history, decent GPS accuracy on the water
apps.weak: Premium often won't unlock after paying, map loads only vegetation or a white screen, no data for many lakes and rivers, few active people in the feed, support hard to reach
apps.whoFor: Anglers who care about depth maps and connecting with others on specific waters, if there's any data for their spot

apps.title: Picture Fish - Fish Identifier
apps.verdict: It half-solves the job: it does okay on simple lake and saltwater fish, but on aquarium fish, especially cichlids, it consistently misses, calling everything a guppy or neon. Beyond identification it offers almost nothing: no species search like its siblings Picture Insect and Picture Mushroom, and anything interesting is locked behind a subscription. Essentially a field guide with no guide.
apps.loved: Recognizes simple lake and saltwater fish, decent info when it guesses right, familiar Picture family brand
apps.weak: Misses on aquarium fish and cichlids, no species search, limited number of IDs, everything behind a subscription
apps.whoFor: Anglers wanting a quick guess at a lake or saltwater catch, not aquarium keepers

quotes.text: This fish ID app is the go to thing, and I don’t think it has ever steered us wrong. Even when we are in the Caribbean or off the Pacific Shores

The very first day I took 21 pictures of my aquarium fish and it got just the simplest of fish correct it miss identified 18 of the 21 photos... likes to call just about everything either an angelfish, a guppy or a goldfish
I was given three options. How am I supposed to know what the actual right one is?

apps.title: Catchr: Fish Identifier
apps.verdict: People genuinely love the idea: logging catches like Pokemon Go, accurate ID, slick design. But the product is half-broken: photo uploads mass-hang on the identification screen, the 'crew' feature doesn't work, and you can't invite friends. On top of that every single feature is locked behind a subscription that isn't flagged at install, and in smaller areas there's often nobody around and the feed is dead.
apps.loved: Logging catches like Pokemon Go, accurate identification, quality design, the collecting thrill
apps.weak: Photo upload hangs on the ID screen, crew feature and friend invites don't work, everything behind a subscription with no warning, empty in small areas
apps.whoFor: Anglers who enjoy building a catch collection and sharing, if they'll pay and live in an active area

quotes.text: I love this app. It’s very fun! But the feature where you can pick a photo you’ve previously taken from your camera roll doesn’t really work. It just loads the “finalising identification” screen and doesn’t go any further.

apps.title: FishHunter - Fish Finder/Sonar
apps.verdict: When it works, the compact sonar finds fish and depth well from a kayak or on ice, and people love casting it out and mapping the bottom. But more often it does not work: the unit will not connect or drops out, connecting takes half an hour, dark mode makes text unreadable, sign-in throws an Error. The app also has not been updated in ages and support ignores emails.
apps.loved: Compact castable sonar for kayak and ice, finding fish and depth from a cast, mapping the bottom and structure, marking fish on screen
apps.weak: Unit will not connect or drops out, connecting takes half an hour, battery lasts 75 minutes, dark mode makes text unreadable, maps cut off with Map too big, sign-in throws an Error, support silent, app long unupdated
apps.whoFor: A kayak or ice angler who wants a castable sonar and can endure the connection problems.

quotes.text: This app and device would be amazing if it stay linked. For the money you pay, you would think the app would be a lot better. I’ve only been able to connect twice.
